content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce Salad is a mix of fresh lettuce leaves and assorted vegetables (cucumber, bell pepper, radish, spring onion, etc.) without tomatoes, carrots, or dressing. It works well as a light snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad is over 90 % water, making it an excellent source of hydration.
Lettuce leaves are rich in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Excluding tomatoes and carrots reduces the amount of lycopene and beta‑carotene, focusing the nutrient profile on leafy greens.
Lettuce Salad is often used as a base for more elaborate restaurant dishes.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The salad provides very few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the leaves and vegetables promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Contains polyphenols and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw vegetables can harbor Salmonella or E. coli; thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Leafy‑green allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain lettuce varieties.

items.title: Digestive discomfort from excess fiber
items.content: Large portions may cause gas or bloating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the lettuce salad immediately after preparation to keep the leaves crisp. Add nuts, seeds, or a lean protein such as chicken, turkey, or tofu for extra substance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Keep the vegetables dry to prevent the leaves from becoming soggy.
